disprot.name: DisProt
disprot.note_growth_since_paper: The original Alderson et al. 2023 paper analyzed 932 human DisProt IDRs as of its own 2023 snapshot; this project's snapshot (2026-08-13) has 1339 human entries, reflecting three years of continued DisProt curation growth.
disprot.api_deviation_from_documented_behavior: The /api/search endpoint's `limit` and `offset` query parameters do NOT paginate when an `organism` filter is present: requests with limit=5, 50, 500, and 2000 (verified directly against the live API) all returned the identical full 1339-entry `data` array with `size: 1339`. scripts/fetch_data.py was written to loop on offset per the original plan, discovered this during the actual fetch (it collected 9,373 = 7 x 1339 duplicate-laden entries from looping), and was corrected to make a single request and deduplicate by disprot_id defensively. This deviation is disclosed here and in docs/research-protocol.md rather than silently worked around.
disprot.ground_truth_region_definition: Only regions with term_namespace == "Structural state" and term_name == "disorder" are used as the positive curated-disorder label. term_namespace == "Structural transition" / term_name == "disorder to order" regions (conditional folding) are recorded separately per protein (is_conditional flag) and used only in the breakdown analysis, never as part of the primary ground-truth label.
disprot.primary_database_citation: DisProt: intrinsically disordered protein database, Nucleic Acids Research (see https://disprot.org for the current release citation; this project cites the database and API, not a specific NAR publication year, because the `release=current` snapshot spans multiple published DisProt releases).

alphafold_db.name: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (EBI)
alphafold_db.confidence_endpoint_pattern: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/files/AF-{accession}-F1-confidence_v{version}.json (the exact URL used per accession is read from each entry's own plddtDocUrl field, not constructed manually)
alphafold_db.api_deviation_from_documented_behavior: The metadata endpoint can return more than one record for a single queried accession, but in the live API (verified 2026-08-13) these additional records are overwhelmingly UniProt ISOFORM entries (e.g. querying O00273 also returns a record whose own uniprotAccession field is "O00273-2", not the long-protein -F1/-F2/-F3 sequence-fragmentation this project originally expected from AlphaFold DB documentation). scripts/fetch_data.py filters returned records to uniprotAccession == the queried accession before deciding an entry is genuinely fragmented; before this fix, the fetch spuriously excluded 250/400 sampled proteins as 'fragmented' when they were in fact single-fragment canonical entries alongside isoform records. After the fix, only 6/400 sampled proteins were genuinely excluded for having more than one exact-accession-matching record.
alphafold_db.primary_citation: Jumper, J., Evans, R., Pritzel, A. et al. Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold. Nature 596, 583-589 (2021). DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2 (verified independently: title, journal, volume/page, year, and DOI resolve correctly).

sample_construction.method: Fixed-seed reproducible random sample of 400 of the 1339 human DisProt entries, numpy.random.default_rng(seed=20260813), sampled without replacement from the entries sorted by disprot_id.

realized_dataset.note: conditional_disorder_residues counts disorder-annotated residues on a protein that ALSO has at least one 'disorder to order' (Structural transition) region annotated somewhere on that same protein — a protein-level proxy for 'looks like it may conditionally fold', not identical to Alderson et al. 2023's own five-database conditionally-folded-IDR definition.

verification.method: structural: DisProt sequence length is required to exactly match the AlphaFold DB uniprotSequence length for the same accession before an entry is included; any mismatch is excluded and logged rather than silently truncated. AlphaFold DB metadata is filtered to exact-accession records before checking for genuine fragmentation.
checks: every included residue's residue_number is drawn directly from the AlphaFold DB confidence JSON's own residueNumber array, not assumed to be a contiguous 1..N range
DisProt region start/end are used as inclusive 1-based bounds, matching both APIs' own indexing convention
0 of 400 sampled entries were excluded for a sequence-length mismatch in this run
verification.enforced_by: scripts/fetch_data.py logs every exclusion with its reason to data/external/exclusions_log.json

raw_file_reason: The joined per-residue table (data/external/joined_residues.csv) is a bounded (387-protein), derived dataset licensed CC BY 4.0 downstream of two CC BY 4.0 sources, and is committed to make the frozen registry byte-reproducible in CI without depending on two live third-party APIs staying available and behaviorally identical on every run (both APIs already showed one undocumented-behavior deviation each during this project's own build, see above). The full raw DisProt fetch cache (data/external/disprot_raw.json, ~12 MB, all 1339 human entries before sampling) is NOT committed — it is a regenerable intermediate cache, not the dataset this project's results are computed from. scripts/fetch_data.py re-fetches and re-joins from live data at reproduction time; running it should reproduce the same 400-entry sample (fixed seed) and, absent upstream data changes, materially the same joined table.
